title: Form reads at the form doors: push the name and package predicates down (SQL first) — residual of #37086 review S5
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · os-alice · session_011y7As8wf3DSPRevwNnYLcM
Filing gate: ① · Source: fleet · finding class b · reach: named producer (`readEffectiveForms` / `readEffectiveFormItem` in `packages/metadata-protocol`, every form read and every anonymous form-door request)

## What

Residual of contract review finding S5 on PR #37422 (card #37086; first recorded in 7184811209, carried through 7203725192). `readEffectiveForms` drops `names` and `packageId` from the request and filters in memory after full reads of both types (`view` and `form`) and of every stored row of both. `readEffectiveFormItem` can call it up to three times for one by-name read, and each anonymous form-door request repeats the view-list and stored-row reads for the form read, the two per-package layers and the unreadable bodies.

## Why its own card

Prime Directive 5 (SQL first): the name and package predicates should be pushed down, or the code should state why the two-type resolution (D5 served-row order across `view` and `form`) cannot take them. #37422 already narrowed part of it in its rework rounds; the seat took the residual out of that PR to land the form type, by the seat's ruling recorded in its ACCEPT 7204181264.

## Acceptance (proposed, for triage)

- A by-name form read and a form-door request read only the rows the name (and package, where given) can resolve to, or the code states, at `readEffectiveForms`, the measured reason it cannot.
- A pin counts the reads for one by-name read and one door request, with a CONTROL.
